title: The A/B Test on One Page

callouts.label: Consent and privacy
callouts.hint: A form with a check mark and a shield above the crowd of students.
callouts.description: Students and families are informed, and student data is protected. The pool is drawn as plain silhouettes with no identifying features.
callouts.tip: Keep names and records out of every prompt and report.

callouts.label: Random assignment
callouts.hint: Four colored tokens being shuffled between a crowd of students and the two lanes.
callouts.description: Students are assigned to the two groups at random, like shuffled tokens. Random assignment spreads motivation and ability evenly, so students do not choose their group.
callouts.tip: Never let volunteers pick a version. Student choice is a confounder.

callouts.label: The control group
callouts.hint: The upper lane, where a group of students uses a plain document, version v1.
callouts.description: The control group uses the original version, v1, with a rubric total of 65 (Revise). It receives ordinary teaching with the original, not no teaching.
callouts.tip: The two lanes are mirror images. The only visible difference is the version.

callouts.label: The hypothesis
callouts.hint: A glowing lightbulb above the two lanes.
callouts.description: The hypothesis states what you expect, such as that the improved version gives a larger learning gain than the original. In the pilot it set a threshold of 5 points.
callouts.tip: Write the hypothesis before the test, so the result cannot choose it.

callouts.label: The treatment group
callouts.hint: The lower lane, where a group of students uses a document with a small upward chevron, version v1.1.
callouts.description: The treatment group uses the improved version, v1.1, with a rubric total of 78 (Adopt). Everything else is the same as for the control group.
callouts.tip: Change one thing at a time, or say that you tested a bundle.

callouts.label: The pre-test
callouts.hint: A sheet with check boxes, at the start of each lane, before the version document.
callouts.description: Both groups take the same pre-test before the lesson, in week 1. It shows where each student starts, so the gain can be measured.
callouts.tip: Use the same test and key for both groups.

callouts.label: The post-test and the learning gain
callouts.hint: A second sheet at the end of each lane, with arrows leading up to two bars of different heights.
callouts.description: Both groups take the same post-test in week 4. The comparison is the learning gain of each group, the post-test score minus the pre-test score.
callouts.tip: A difference from a small test may partly be luck. Chapter 17 puts it in context with an effect size.
